subject.title: Add retry logic to OAuth token refresh

question: Which OAuth refresh failures are safe to retry across providers, and what maximum added latency should the shared agent request path permit?
rationale: Current adapters do not expose a confirmed provider-neutral transient-error contract, while unconditional retries could repeat permanent credential failures and delay every affected agent request.

options.title: Shared classified retry
options.body: Define a narrow transient-error classifier and bounded shared retry budget, with provider hooks for errors that cannot be classified generically.

options.title: Provider-owned retries
options.body: Keep the shared manager single-shot and require each OAuth adapter to implement and test its own retry policy.

options.title: Retain single-shot behavior
options.body: Continue relying on credential adoption, provider fallback, and re-authentication rather than adding retry latency to the shared path.

recommendation.title: Shared classified retry
recommendation.body: Define a narrow transient-error classifier and bounded shared retry budget, with provider hooks for errors that cannot be classified generically.

likelyOwner.reason: The feature history most strongly connects this person to the shared OAuth manager boundary and its current recovery policy.
